title: The Missing Field Notes
intro: At 7:12 this morning, a field notebook arrived without its final page. Its author, Mira, left three clues: a branching line, a repeated mark, and a place where the ground changes. Your task is to reconstruct what she was studying. This is a fictional case. The evidence you collect is real.

clues.title: The branching line
clues.subject: leaf
clues.task: Find a fallen leaf. Look closely at its veins. Describe how the smaller lines connect to the main vein.
clues.prompt: Do the veins branch from one main line, spread from one point, or run alongside each other? It is fine if you cannot tell.
clues.audio: First entry. Mira drew a line that splits, and splits again. Find a fallen leaf on your familiar walk. Study its veins without picking a living plant. What pattern do you see? Take one photograph and a short note, then put your phone away.
clues.reveal: The first note reads: 'A path can divide without losing its direction.' Mira was recording patterns, not a destination.
clues.hint: Look at a large fallen leaf in even light. Photograph its surface close enough to see the veins.

clues.title: The repeated mark
clues.subject: tree bark
clues.task: Find a tree along the same familiar path. Observe its bark without removing or marking it. Look for one repeating feature.
clues.prompt: Describe ridges, cracks, flakes, or another pattern you can actually see.
clues.audio: Second entry. A witness remembers the same mark appearing over and over. Look at the bark of a nearby tree. Are there ridges, cracks, or flakes? Leave the bark where it is. Record one repeated feature. The next part of the story can wait while you look.
clues.reveal: The second note reads: 'What looks like a single surface holds many smaller stories.' Mira was looking closer each time.
clues.hint: Use a tree you can reach from your public path. A close photo of the trunk is enough.

clues.title: The changing ground
clues.subject: ground surface
clues.task: Compare two nearby patches of ground: one beneath a tree and one more exposed. Stay on your familiar path.
clues.prompt: What visible difference do you notice: fallen leaves, colour, texture, or cover? Record uncertainty rather than guessing moisture or temperature.
clues.audio: Final entry. Mira wrote that two places, only a few steps apart, can tell different stories. Compare the ground under a tree with an exposed patch nearby. Look for a visible difference in leaves, colour, texture, or cover. Do not infer temperature or moisture from a photograph. This is the last clue. Return with what you really observed.
clues.reveal: The final note reads: 'The missing page is the one you write yourself.' Mira left room for another observer.
clues.hint: Put both patches in one photograph if possible. If there is no visible difference, that is a valid observation.

complete.title: The page was yours all along.
complete.text: Mira's notes were an invitation to notice. Your three observations complete the notebook. The mystery ends here; the patterns are still outside.

open.title: Some pages stay open.
open.text: You returned with observations and honest uncertainty. The notebook is still unfinished, and that is a useful result. Keep what you noticed; revisit a clue another day if you want.

branching.title: The network sketch
branching.text: In the fiction, Mira drew a branching network rather than a route. The missing page may connect separate observations.

fan.title: The meeting point
fan.text: In the fiction, Mira drew several lines meeting at one point. The missing page may bring several viewpoints together.

parallel.title: The ruled page
parallel.text: In the fiction, Mira copied lines running alongside one another. Her sketch may be a page layout rather than a map.

unclear.title: An unreadable sketch
unclear.text: The sketch stays unresolved. An unclear observation does not need a confident explanation.

ridged.title: The repeated signal
ridged.text: In the fiction, Mira used repeated ridges as a rhythm: separate marks belonging to one record.

flaky.title: The layered archive
flaky.text: In the fiction, the repeating mark refers to layers. Mira may have hidden a newer entry beneath an older one.

smooth.title: The missing mark
smooth.text: In the fiction, the surface offers no strong repeating relief. The witness may have remembered a mark that was never there.

unclear.title: The witness remains uncertain
unclear.text: The witness account stays open. Record what is visible and leave the rest unwritten.

covered.title: The scattered pages
covered.text: In the fiction, visible ground cover becomes Mira’s scattered pages. Her final record belongs to the things that gather here.

bare.title: The exposed page
bare.text: In the fiction, a visibly more exposed patch becomes a blank page. The absent record was an invitation to add an observation.

similar.title: The false contrast
similar.text: In the fiction, the two patches do not offer a clear contrast. Mira’s last clue tests whether you can resist inventing a difference.

unclear.title: The comparison stays open
unclear.text: The final comparison remains unresolved. Another view may help; a guess will not.
